long_biography.plain_text:
Relational analytics gave Michael J. Saylor a distinct place in business software. After studying aeronautics, system dynamics and computer simulation at MIT, he applied modelling experience from industrial consulting to Strategy, the company he founded in 1989. Its software turned large corporate datasets into decision tools, while his inventions later extended across web, mobile and cloud analytics.

Education became another enduring outlet for Saylor’s interest in distributing information. He established Saylor University to provide open online courses without tuition, while his writing examined the effects of mobile computing. After three decades as chief executive, he moved to executive chairman to concentrate on Strategy’s Bitcoin acquisition policy and advocacy.
